task: Sort 15 real companies into fit / no fit as licensors for Lindus Therapeutics, with a one-line reason. 10 passed our checks, 5 failed them.

runs.label: Haiku 4.5
runs.output:
| Company | Fit? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream Bio | No fit | $261.3M cash, clear runway through Phase 3, and no partnering plans announced. |
| Corbus Pharmaceuticals | Fit | Phase 1b obesity data, Phase 2 planned H1 2027, likely needs capital for parallel oncology trial. |
| Mithra Pharmaceuticals | No fit | Bankrupt; assets acquired by Gedeon Richter in 2024. |
| Pila Pharma | Fit | Two Phase 2a trials done, EMA approval for obesity trial, analysts assume more capital needed. |
| Reviva Pharmaceuticals | Fit | Phase 3 completed, FDA requesting second Phase 3, financing contingent, actively pursuing partnerships. |
| Terns Pharmaceuticals | No fit | Being acquired by Merck; decision-making no longer theirs. |
| Skye Bioscience | Fit | Phase 2a obesity completed, merging with Redx, nimacimab to be divested or partnered. |
| Palatin Technologies | No fit | First IND expected Q4 2026; no human clinical data yet. |
| Dermata Therapeutics | No fit | Withdrew IND and paused acne drug program in 2025-2026; asset no longer active. |
| Neumora Therapeutics | No fit | Lead drug failed Phase 3; $147M cash to Q3 2027; no partnering plans announced. |
| Vistagen | Fit | Fasedienol failed Phase 3, refisolone Phase 2-ready, newly appointed Chief Corporate Development Officer signaling openness to licensing. |
| D&D Pharmatech | Fit | Phase 2 MASH data positive (May 2026), China rights out, CEO explicitly says aiming to sign licensing deal by year-end. |
| Connect Biopharma | Fit | Phase 2 asthma efficacy data (Sep 2026), $31.5M cash (~1 year runway), needs Phase 3 funding. |
| Yarrow Bioscience | Fit | Legacy dermatology BET inhibitors in Phase 1b/2 with psoriasis signal; company signals assets may be sold or licensed. |
| Aclaris Therapeutics | No fit | Cash to end of 2028; pursuing partnerships only for respiratory programs outside China, not seeking external funding. |
runs.verdict: Fastest and cheapest; called a shelved asset and a partner-seeker no fit

runs.label: Opus 5.5
runs.output:
| Company | Fit? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream Bio | No fit | Has $261.3M and runway through 2027 to run its own Phase 3s, with no partnering plans announced. |
| Corbus Pharmaceuticals | No fit | Plans to run the obesity Phase 2 itself, with no stated cash gap or partner search; priority is a registrational oncology trial. |
| Mithra Pharmaceuticals | No fit | Went bankrupt in 2024, and Gedeon Richter acquired its estetrol assets. |
| Pila Pharma | Fit | Obesity/T2D drug has two Phase 2a trials done and only part of the next trial funded, so more capital is needed. |
| Reviva Pharmaceuticals | Fit | Schizophrenia Phase 3 depends on new financing; the company moved to OTCQB and is openly pursuing partnerships. |
| Terns Pharmaceuticals | No fit | Merck is acquiring it, so the metabolic assets are no longer its decision. |
| Skye Bioscience | Fit | Obesity antibody has Phase 2a data and will be divested or partnered after the company refocuses on fibrosis. |
| Palatin Technologies | No fit | Targets rare genetic obesities and has no human data on the new molecules. |
| Dermata Therapeutics | Fit | Acne drug has positive Phase 3 data, but the program is paused after the pivot to consumer skincare. |
| Neumora Therapeutics | No fit | Is funding its own next Phase 2 into Q3 2027 and has announced no partnering plans. |
| Vistagen | Fit | Has a Phase 2-ready menopausal hot-flash drug after its lead drug missed Phase 3, cash only into 2027, and a new licensing-focused BD chief. |
| D&D Pharmatech | Fit | MASH drug hit its Phase 2 endpoints, and the company is actively seeking a licensee for rights outside China. |
| Connect Biopharma | Fit | Has a positive Phase 2 in acute asthma attacks but only about one year of cash, and needs a Phase 3 next. |
| Yarrow Bioscience (formerly VYNE) | Fit | Legacy dermatology BET inhibitor with a Phase 1b psoriasis signal may be sold or licensed after the merger (note the partial clinical hold). |
| Aclaris Therapeutics | Fit | Has Phase 1b/2 asthma and atopic dermatitis assets and says it is seeking partners for respiratory programs outside China. |
runs.verdict: Caught every trap; disputed Corbus with the clearest, most careful reasons

takeaway: All three models caught every disqualifier: the Merck buyout, the bankruptcy, the cash-rich companies and the rare-disease focus. Haiku lost two real fits because it read "program paused" and "funded but seeking partners" as reasons to walk away, which is backwards for an in-licenser. Sonnet and Opus only disagreed with our key on Corbus, and they have a point: the line shows a fresh readout but no stated cash gap or partner search, so our "fit" was a timing judgement. Sonnet matched Opus for about half the price, so it is the default for sorting; use Haiku only as a first pass with a human reading its no-fits.
